documents.title: Sores on my fingers
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Since around November my fingers go white and then kind of blue when it's cold out, I thought it was just from working outside all winter. Now I have little sores on a few fingertips that won't heal and hurt like crazy, and a couple on my toes. Also my feet and hands ache when I've been walking around the site a while, goes away if I sit. Sending a picture.

documents.title: RE: Sores on my fingers
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the photo - I want to see these in person. Booked you Tuesday 4/9 at 7:40. Keep them clean and covered, and keep your hands and feet warm.

orders.reason: Digital ulcers and extremity claudication in a heavy smoker

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
36M with ADPKD, AATD/emphysema, heavy smoker. Here for hand and foot symptoms.

HPI: About five months of fingers blanching white then dusky blue in the cold. Over the last couple of months, painful sores at several fingertips and a couple of toe tips that won't heal. Hands and feet ache after walking around the site, settles with rest. No joint pain or swelling, no rash, no fever, no weight loss, no dry eyes or mouth, no heartburn or trouble swallowing. Smoking about 1.5 ppd - went back up over the winter.

Meds: albuterol prn. Ibuprofen occasionally for the finger pain. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Shallow, punched-out ulcers at the tips of several fingers on both hands and two toes; no infection, no drainage. Fingers cool. Skin over fingers not thickened. Radial pulses present but weak; dorsalis pedis faint bilaterally. Cap refill sluggish. No joint synovitis.

A/P
Digital ischemic ulcers with cold-induced color change and limb claudication in a 36 y/o heavy smoker without diabetes or high cholesterol - thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger) is the leading concern. Checking A1c, lipids, ESR, CRP and ANA to look for other causes. Urgent vascular surgery referral.
Ulcer care: wash daily, petrolatum and a dry dressing, gloves and warm socks. Return or text for redness, spreading, or any dark/black skin.
Smoking: told him plainly that if this is Buerger, stopping completely is what saves the fingers and toes - even a few cigarettes keep it going. He was shaken. Nicotine patches/gum are not a good choice here; varenicline is. He wants to talk to the surgeon first.
Acetaminophen better than ibuprofen for the pain.

documents.title: Test results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Results: no diabetes (A1c 5.3), cholesterol normal, inflammation markers normal and the autoimmune screen (ANA) negative. That makes the smoking-related artery problem we talked about more likely. Vascular surgery has you on May 20 - the soonest they had. If any sore turns black, or a finger goes cold and won't warm up, call that day.

documents.title: Vascular surgery consultation
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
VASCULAR SURGERY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 05/20/2024
Referring: primary care

HPI: 36-year-old man referred by his primary care physician (who also follows his ADPKD and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with emphysema, the latter managed by pulmonology). For roughly six months he has had pain in both hands and both feet that comes on with walking and eases at rest, painful sores at several fingertips, and fingers that turn white and then blue in cold weather. No fever, no joint pains, no weight loss.

PMH: ADPKD (normal kidney function, followed by nephrology); alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with emphysema. No diabetes, hypertension or hyperlipidemia.
PSH: tonsillectomy in childhood.
Meds: albuterol inhaler prn; ibuprofen prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father ADPKD with ESRD; mother emphysema/COPD (ex-smoker); older brother AATD.
SH: cigarettes 1.5 packs/day for 15 years, 22.5 pack-years. No alcohol. Construction laborer.

Vitals: T 36.8 C (98.2 F), BP 124/78, HR 76, RR 14.
Exam: shallow ulcerations at the tips of several fingers and several toes, bilaterally. No joint swelling or erythema. Radial and dorsalis pedis pulses diminished on both sides. Capillary refill delayed in fingers and toes. Remainder of the exam unremarkable.

PCP labs April 2024: A1c 5.3, lipids normal, ESR/CRP normal, ANA negative.

Impression: thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger disease) - young heavy smoker, distal upper and lower limb ischemia with digital ulceration, no atherosclerotic risk factors, autoimmune screen negative.

Plan:
1. Complete abstinence from all tobacco and nicotine products. This is the treatment. Without it, progression and amputation risk are high. Discussed in detail; varenicline through PCP would be appropriate, not nicotine replacement.
2. Local wound care: daily cleansing, nonadherent dressing; protect from cold and trauma.
3. Arteriography of the hands and feet to confirm the pattern; scheduled.
4. Follow-up one year, sooner for any nonhealing or worsening ulcer.

NKDA.
Vascular Surgery

documents.title: Vascular surgery letter - arteriogram
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
VASCULAR SURGERY - INTERVAL LETTER
Re: arteriography 06/06/2024

Upper and lower extremity arteriography was performed via right common femoral access without complication.
Findings: proximal arteries of both arms and legs are smooth with no atherosclerotic plaque and no source of emboli. There are segmental occlusions of the digital arteries of both hands and of the distal tibial arteries of both legs, with corkscrew collateral vessels around the occlusions.
Conclusion: findings typical of thromboangiitis obliterans. No lesion suitable for revascularization.

Plan unchanged: total tobacco abstinence, wound care, follow-up in a year.
NKDA.
Vascular Surgery

documents.title: Arteriogram letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Confirms Buerger. Video visit booked to go over it and push cessation again.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt in his truck after work, two identifiers confirmed.

Went over vascular consult and arteriogram: Buerger disease confirmed. He'd looked it up and seen the amputation pictures. Says he's down to about a pack a day. Finger sores a little smaller with summer and the dressings; one toe still open but clean.

We talked through varenicline for 20 minutes - side effects, how it's taken. He still doesn't want a medicine, "I want to do it myself." No nicotine products (explained why). Wants the quitline call-back - referral sent.

A/P
1. Buerger disease - vascular following, wound care per their plan.
2. Tobacco use disorder - ~1 ppd, declines pharmacotherapy, quitline referral.
3. AATD/emphysema - pulm in August.
4. ADPKD - nephrology in the fall.
Text me photos of the toe if it changes.

reports.text: Good effort, reproducible. Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.61. FEV1 70% of predicted. FVC normal.

documents.title: Pulmonology follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY FOLLOW-UP
Visit 08/21/2024

Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (ZZ) with basilar emphysema. Since last year he has also been diagnosed with Buerger disease by vascular surgery. He reports smoking about a pack a day. Exertional breathlessness unchanged; albuterol on most workdays. No exacerbations, no hospital visits.

Spirometry: FEV1/FVC 0.61, FEV1 70% predicted (71% in 2023).
Exam: diminished breath sounds at both bases, no wheeze.

Assessment: stable lung function over a year, still smoking.
Plan: augmentation remains deferred until he has stopped smoking. Continue albuterol as needed. Vaccines per PCP. Yearly hepatic panel per PCP. Return 1 year.
NKDA.
Pulmonology

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
NEPHROLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit 10/02/2024

ADPKD. Interval Buerger disease diagnosis (vascular surgery, arteriogram 6/2024). Still smoking ~1 ppd.
Home BP fine. Office BP 124/78.
Creatinine 1.3 today (1.25 in 2023, 1.2 in 2022).
Meds: albuterol prn. Still takes ibuprofen now and then for pain - asked him again to stop it entirely.
NKDA.

Assessment: ADPKD with slowly rising creatinine, still within normal range, normotensive.
Plan: unchanged. Labs with PCP, return 1 year.
Nephrology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, 36M.

Problems: ADPKD (Cr 1.3 at nephrology this month, normotensive); AATD ZZ with emphysema (FEV1 70% in Aug, augmentation deferred while smoking); Buerger disease (vascular, arteriogram June); tobacco use disorder.

Interval: finger and toe sores healed over the summer. Cold weather coming and he's nervous about it - has heated gloves now. Breathing stable. Smoking "a pack, some days less." Quitline called twice, he didn't call back. Pain: an ibuprofen "maybe once every couple weeks."

NKDA. Meds: albuterol prn, ibuprofen OTC rare.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs diminished at bases, no wheeze. Heart RRR. Abdomen: kidneys palpable. Hands: healed scars at several fingertips, no open ulcer; fingers cool. Feet: toes intact, healed tips, DP faint bilat. No edema.

Plan: CMP, CBC, UACR. Flu + updated COVID today. PHQ-2 1. Tobacco: offered varenicline once more - no. Keep extremities warm, check feet daily. Any new sore: text a photo.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine in line with nephrology's 1.3. Liver tests normal. CBC normal. UACR normal. Released.
